featured_reviews.review_text:
Chadha’s is unapologetically rich, buttery, and incredibly flavorful.
The Food Rundown:
• Amritsari Aloo Pyaaz Kulcha Combo: The star of the meal. The kulcha was perfectly crisp on the outside with a generous, spiced filling. When paired with the chole, it’s easily one of the best versions of this dish in the suburbs.
• Malai Chaap: This was melt-in-your-mouth tender. It’s prepared in a thick, velvety cream sauce that is pure indulgence.
• Aloo Tikki: A great starter with a satisfying crunch and the right balance of tangy chutneys.
• Jalebi & Rabdi Combo: You cannot leave without this. The jalebis were hot and syrupy, and the rabdi was thick and traditional—the perfect way to end the meal on a high note.
The Experience:
The food is undeniably heavy on butter and ghee, which makes it taste fantastic but definitely sits heavy on the stomach. It’s the kind of meal where you’ll want a long nap afterward! The portions are generous and the flavors are consistent.
Verdict: A must-visit for anyone who loves authentic North Indian street food. Just come with a massive appetite and a plan to take it easy for the rest of the day.

Later, I found both the Paneer Tikka and an unordered 'Chur Chur Naan' on my bill.
​Management’s Response:
When I took the bill to the counter, I instantly raised my concern. They were ready to cut the items from the bill just to end the discussion, but the owner/manager laughed it off as a "simple mistake." To me, this felt like a deliberate attempt to inflate the bill. If an item isn't in the digital system, it shouldn't be on the table or the bill.
​My Message to the Owner:
I paid the full amount, including the items I didn't order, because I value my principles. I want you to understand that your food is great, but your staff needs serious training. Please invest in educated, professional staff who understand transparency and honest order-taking. This "mistake" shouldn't happen to any other customer.

featured_reviews.name: Deepa Thathagar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, on the last Sunday, my husband and I decided to go out for dinner. We thought of trying a new restaurant nearby.

We chose The Fillo, a recently opened restaurant in Bhayandar West. Excited about visiting the place, and considering it was a weekend, we decided to reach early to avoid waiting. However, our excitement quickly turned into disappointment, resulting in one of the worst dining experiences we’ve ever had.

When we arrived, they informed us that all the tables were occupied and asked us to wait for 30 minutes. We had reached at 7:45 PM, but even after waiting, we didn’t get a table. The host insisted we sit in the garden area, which was vacant. However, we had clearly mentioned that we preferred an AC table and were willing to wait. This made me feel quite awkward—if we had already requested an AC table, why were they trying to force us into the garden area?

To make matters worse, we noticed a group of four people arrive without a reservation, yet they were promptly offered an AC table. When we questioned the host and the manager, they claimed the table was for four people and not for two. My husband and I were furious with this illogical reasoning. After arguing with them, they apologized and eventually arranged a table of six for us.

Once seated, barely 5–7 minutes passed before a staff member approached us and asked us to move to a smaller table for two so they could accommodate another family of 4–5 people. While we agreed to cooperate, we couldn’t help but feel undervalued as customers. Regardless of whether there are two or four diners, everyone is paying for their meal, and this kind of treatment felt discriminatory.

While seated at the table for two, we observed the staff moving another family from a table for six to a table for four, just to accommodate others. The constant shuffling of guests between tables was chaotic and showed a complete lack of management.

The food, unfortunately, didn’t make up for the poor service. The menu was limited, and the dishes we tried were disappointing:

Cheese Fries: Served in a strainer, causing all the liquid cheese to drain off. The fries were dry and lacked flavor. When we complained, they apologized and served cheese separately, but by then, the taste was already ruined.

Chur Chur Naan: This was essentially a crumbled potato paratha with no distinctive flavor or masala.

Pesto Bao: While new and somewhat acceptable, it wasn’t impressive.

Frustrated, we gave up and didn’t order anything else. The overall experience felt like a complete waste of time and money. In hindsight, we should’ve gone to one of our usual dining spots where we’re always satisfied with the meal and service.

I will never recommend The Fillo, even if someone offers to take you there for free or as part of a party.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Kharbe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Parotha definitely impressed me with its authentic South Indian flavors. I tried the nool parotha with chicken curry, and it was absolutely delicious — soft, well-layered, and paired perfectly with the rich, flavorful curry. For starters, the chicken 65 was crispy and spicy just the way it should be, while the chicken sukha had a nice dry masala coating that tasted amazing.
I also had the Kerala parotha with chicken curry, and it was equally satisfying — flaky, buttery, and fresh. Overall, the food quality and taste were really good, and the variety makes it worth visiting.
Giving it 4 stars because while the food was great, there’s still a little room for improvement in consistency or service. But definitely a place I’d come back to!

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Patra
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a good experience at Madras Parota. The parathas were fresh, soft, and full of flavor without being too oily. Portions were satisfying and the prices felt reasonable. Service was quick, and the food tasted homely and comforting. A nice place for a simple, filling meal when you’re craving South Indian style food.

featured_reviews.name: syed yusuf
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved the Tamil Nadu–style food here! The parotta with chicken salna was soft, flaky, and full of authentic flavor. The kulambu kalaki was a real highlight—rich, spicy gravy with perfectly cooked eggs, true comfort food.

The chicken Chettinad chukka was spicy, well-roasted, and packed with bold masalas. Both the chicken killi parotta and chicken kothu parotta were fresh, flavorful, and felt just like classic South Indian street food. Even the dosa was crisp and well-made.

Ending the meal with filter coffee was the perfect touch—strong, aromatic, and very satisfying. Simple place, amazing taste, and real Tamil Nadu vibes. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Shubham Raut
featured_reviews.review_text: Best of the foods are often found in less premium places! This place might not be shiny and glittery but the food is absolutely worth it! Had mutton biriyani, single chicken omelette and parota and everything was super tasty! Mutton biriyani highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Rathinavel Dravidar
featured_reviews.review_text: Finally, authentic taste has arrived in Mira Road! It felt great knowing that the long journey to Dharavi is no longer needed. Madras Porata offers really good service with truly authentic flavors. A must-visit place and definitely good to go for South Indian food lovers.
